content: Hey, I am looking for advice for #40941. I designed a local notion of stabilizer in Representation. The motivation is to shorten the presentation in the discussion of smooth representations where we have to prove various openness of stabilizers. In mathlib, many representation theory materials only require G to be a Monoid. It is indeed natural to require G to be a monoid in the most part of stabilizer.lean (except for the last lemma stabilizer_conj which involves the conjugate subgroup). However, for smooth representation theory, it is crucial for G to be a TopologicalGroup from the very begining, rather than TopologicalMonoid. If I require G to be a Monoid in Representation.stabilizer, then my stabilizer becomes a submonoid, which is not ideal to prove openness (in fact, impossible without refering to the group structure). Is there any suggestion to help meet both generality and application?

Generalizing to Monoid is great when it's free, but here it would force you down from Subgroup to Submonoid which isn't ideal. Note that docs#MulAction.stabilizer also uses Subgroups, so I think you're in good company here.
